name: Balancer
description:
Chooses one endpoint for a call.

`pick` is synchronous and returns an error-first tuple. It does not throw
for an empty candidate list. A selected endpoint is one of the candidates
supplied to that pick.

typeTable.name: pick
typeTable.description:
Selects an endpoint synchronously, or returns an error when none can be selected.
Must be synchronous.

name: Client
description:
Client value that operations accept.

A client value carries the base configuration and one call's request options. Operations accept it. It is not callable; create one by calling the factory returned by `createClient`. Calling a client value throws a `TypeError` at runtime and fails to compile.

Create a client value per call. Reusing a value that carries `signal` shares that signal between calls.

typeTable.name: [CLIENT]
typeTable.description: Internal state. Not part of the call surface.

name: ClientConfig
description:
Resolved client configuration after option helpers have been applied.

The snapshot that `createClient` builds, that every option helper mutates, and that instances from `createClient` hold.

Before any option applies, `endpoints` is `[]`, `balancer` is a new `pickFirstBalancer()`, `interceptors` is empty, `retry` is undefined (retries disabled), and `http.handle` and `sse.handle` share a default wrapper that resolves `globalThis.fetch` on each call. Replacing Fetch after import affects both defaults. Core can be imported without Fetch; a default HTTP/SSE execution fails with `ENV_UNSUPPORTED` if it is still missing. Custom handles do not require a global Fetch. `webSocket.handle` is `globalThis.WebSocket`, and the other `webSocket` settings are unset. `finalizeHeaders` stays unset; `@defjs/core/xsrf` assigns it for browser XSRF forwarding.

typeTable.name: endpoints
typeTable.description:
Candidate base URLs in first-seen order. Empty until `withEndpoint` runs.
The balancer picks one per call.

typeTable.name: headers
typeTable.description: Static default headers merged under headers returned by the builder for HTTP/SSE.

typeTable.name: http
typeTable.description: HTTP transport with a required fetch handle.

typeTable.name: interceptors
typeTable.description: Interceptors applied in registration order.

typeTable.name: querySerializer
typeTable.description: Serializes encoded query objects. Omit to use `URLSearchParams`.

typeTable.name: finalizeHeaders
typeTable.description:
Called once per HTTP attempt. The hook receives the outgoing headers after interceptors and before the default `Accept` is filled in, plus the resolved URL.
A throw fails the call with `EXT_HOOK_FAILED`, with the thrown value as `cause`. It is not an endpoint attempt and is not retried. Stays unset until an option assigns it.
typeTable.type: ((request: HttpRequest, headers: Headers, url: URL) => void) | undefined

typeTable.name: withCredentials
typeTable.description: When `true`, credentials are included with requests.

typeTable.name: balancer
typeTable.description: Selects one candidate per call. Defaults to a fresh pickFirstBalancer.

typeTable.name: retry
typeTable.description: Retry policy shared by HTTP, SSE, and WebSocket. Unset means every call makes one attempt.

typeTable.name: sse
typeTable.description: Resolved SSE configuration.

typeTable.name: webSocket

name: ClientOption

Function type of the option helpers accepted by `createClient`.

Mutates the {@link ClientConfig} that `createClient` is building. Every `with*` helper returns one. `createClient` applies the options in order, so a later option overwrites an earlier one for the same setting, except `withInterceptors`, which appends.

name: ClientOptions
description:
Input-shaped client options, including SSE and WebSocket, that mirror what the option helpers configure.

The user-facing shape of the settings before defaults are applied. `createClient` does not accept this object; configure a client with option helpers such as `withEndpoint`. {@link ClientConfig} is the resolved counterpart.

typeTable.description:
Candidate base URLs. `withEndpoint` copies them and drops later duplicates.
An empty list is legal and fails at execution with `REQ_BUILD_FAILED`.

typeTable.name: headers

typeTable.name: http

typeTable.name: interceptors

typeTable.name: withCredentials
typeTable.description: When `true`, credentials are included with requests.

typeTable.description: Opt-in retry policy shared by HTTP, SSE, and WebSocket.

name: ClientSSEConfig
description:
Resolved SSE configuration with a required fetch handle.

The type of `ClientConfig.sse`. It is {@link ClientSSEOptions} with `handle` always present; the default wrapper resolves the current global `fetch` on each attempt, rather than capturing it at import time.

typeTable.name: handle
typeTable.description: Fetch implementation used to open the event stream.

typeTable.name: onInvalidEvent
typeTable.description: Called when an event has no matching struct or fails validation.
typeTable.type: ((context: { reason: "missing-struct" | "validation-failed"; message: { id: string; event: string; data: string; }; cause?: unknown; signal: AbortSignal; }) => unknown) | undefined

name: ClientSSEOptions
description:
Optional SSE settings applied when creating a client: fetch handle and invalid-event hook.

- **handle** — Fetch implementation that opens the stream. The default resolves `globalThis.fetch` on each attempt, including replacements installed after import. Every SSE handle receives a `Request`. Missing global Fetch fails default execution with `ENV_UNSUPPORTED`; a custom handle remains usable.
- **onInvalidEvent** — Called when an event has no matching struct and no `default` struct (`'missing-struct'`), or its data fails validation (`'validation-failed'`). The event is skipped. An error thrown by the hook does not close the stream.

Set these with `withSSEHandle` and `withSSEOnInvalidEvent`. Retries come from the client's `retry` policy, set with `withRetry`; without one a failed stream is not retried.

typeTable.name: handle
typeTable.description: Fetch implementation used to open the event stream; defaults to resolving global `fetch` on each call.

typeTable.name: onInvalidEvent
typeTable.description: Called when an event has no matching struct or fails validation.
typeTable.type: ((context: { reason: "missing-struct" | "validation-failed"; message: { id: string; event: string; data: string; }; cause?: unknown; signal: AbortSignal; }) => unknown) | undefined

name: ClientWebSocketOptions
description:
Optional WebSocket settings applied when creating a client: constructor, `beforeConnect` hook, heartbeat, and protocols.

- **handle** — WebSocket constructor; defaults to `globalThis.WebSocket`.
- **beforeConnect** — Runs before each connect and reconnect attempt.
- **heartbeat** — Sends `message()` every `intervalMs`. With `timeoutMs` and `isAck`, a missing acknowledgement counts as a connection failure and reports `NET_UNREACHABLE` to the balancer. See {@link WebSocketHeartbeatConfig}.
- **protocols** — Subprotocols passed to the constructor.

Set these with `withWebSocketHandle`, `withWebSocketBeforeConnect`, `withWebSocketHeartbeat`, and `withWebSocketProtocols`. `WebSocketExecuteOptions` can override `beforeConnect`, `heartbeat`, and `protocols` per call. Reconnection comes from the client's `retry` policy, set with `withRetry`; without one a close ends the session.

typeTable.name: handle
typeTable.description: WebSocket constructor; defaults to `globalThis.WebSocket`.

typeTable.name: beforeConnect
typeTable.description: Hook before each connect/reconnect attempt.
typeTable.type: ((context: { attempt: number; signal: AbortSignal; }) => void | Promise<void>) | undefined

typeTable.name: heartbeat
typeTable.description: Periodic heartbeat message and optional acknowledgement matching.

typeTable.name: protocols
typeTable.description: Subprotocols passed to the WebSocket constructor.

name: DerivableClient
description:
Callable root client returned by `createClient`.

A factory is a {@link Client} that carries no request options, so it can be passed to an operation directly. Calling it with {@link RequestOptions} returns a plain, non-callable `Client` value for one call and performs no I/O. That value cannot be called again: `client()()` fails to compile and throws a `TypeError` at runtime. `client()` and `client(undefined)` store no request options. `client({})` keeps the empty snapshot produced by reading each top-level field; it is not dropped by inspecting keys.

Each provided field is read once, in declaration order, onto a new options object. A `protocols` array is copied. `heartbeat` copies `intervalMs`, `isAck`, `message`, and `timeoutMs`. `retry` copies `maxRetries`, `delayMs`, `factor`, `maxDelayMs`, `jitter`, `attemptTimeoutMs`, `methods` and `statusCodes` arrays, `retryAfter`, `maxRetryAfterMs`, `shouldRetry`, and `budget`. Missing nested blocks stay `undefined` and do not enable heartbeat or retry. `signal`, `beforeConnect`, and every callback keep their identity. A getter on these fixed fields runs during the call. If it throws, the exception escapes and is not converted into a fault; the factory stays usable.

typeTable.name: [CLIENT]
typeTable.description: Internal state. Not part of the call surface.

name: DoneInfo
description:
Outcome of the attempt that used the selected endpoint.

`attempted: false` means no attempt is attributed to that endpoint: nothing
was sent, the attempt ended by caller cancellation or `close()`, or `fetch`
rejected a streamed HTTP request body with a network error before any
response. Both `code` and `status` are then absent. `attempted: true` with no
`code` means the peer answered without a classified failure. Built-in balancers
read only the neutral `code`, never `status`.

A streamed HTTP request body is a caller-supplied `ReadableStream`. `fetch`
rejects it with the same network error for a refused connection, an HTTP/1.1 connection, a redirect that cannot
replay the stream, a failed CORS preflight, and a source stream that throws,
so that error does not reliably show the endpoint is down and is reported as
`{ attempted: false }`. The cost is that a genuinely down endpoint is not
detected by streamed uploads alone: they do not switch `pickFirst` away from
it and do not count toward `outlierDetection`.

typeTable.name: attempted
typeTable.description: Whether a transport attempt reached the selected endpoint.

typeTable.name: code
typeTable.description: Neutral attempt outcome, including failures after a peer response begins.

typeTable.name: status
typeTable.description: Raw response status for custom balancers; built-in balancers never read it.

name: ERR_NO_CANDIDATE
description:
Sentinel for an empty candidate list.

Built-in balancers return it as `[ERR_NO_CANDIDATE, undefined]`. The runtime
reports that as `REQ_BUILD_FAILED` and keeps this error as `cause`. It is not
a `FaultCode`. The non-enumerable `Symbol.for("defjs.cause.no-endpoint")`
brand lets {@link isNoCandidateCause} recognize the sentinel from another
Core copy.

overloads.signature: const ERR_NO_CANDIDATE: Error;

name: FetchHandle
description:
Fetch-compatible function used as an HTTP or SSE handle.

This is the `(input, init?) => Promise<Response>` call signature Defjs invokes, deliberately not `typeof fetch`, so a mock does not need host extras such as `preconnect`. HTTP calls the untouched platform Fetch as `(url, init)`; a replaced global Fetch or custom handle receives a `Request`. The default resolves the global on each call. SSE always passes a `Request`, including to its default handle.

When an HTTP or SSE call through the client rejects with a value that is not a cancellation or timeout shape, the client reports `NET_UNREACHABLE`, whether the value is an `Error` or not. A call with a retry policy can then retry it. `fetchHandler` rejects with the value as is.

Accepted by `withHTTPHandle`, `withSSEHandle`, and `fetchHandler`.

name: HttpRetryContext
description:
What `shouldRetry` receives after a failed HTTP attempt.

`cause` is the fault the attempt returned. `status` is the response status when the attempt got a response, and `headers` holds its response headers. `retryAfterMs` is present for a `429` or `503` response carrying a valid RFC 9110 `Retry-After` header when `retryAfter` is enabled. `retryable` is `true` for a method in `methods` and a failure without a response, a status in `statusCodes` (429, 502, 503, or 504 by default), or an attempt timeout.

typeTable.name: method
typeTable.description: Method the attempt sent. It is the last one when an interceptor sent more than one request.

typeTable.name: endpoint
typeTable.description: Endpoint the failed attempt used.

typeTable.name: status
typeTable.description: Status of the response, when the attempt got one.

typeTable.name: headers
typeTable.description: Response headers, when the attempt got a response.

typeTable.name: retryAfterMs
typeTable.description: Parsed RFC 9110 `Retry-After` delay in milliseconds for a `429` or `503` response when `retryAfter` is enabled.

typeTable.name: attempt
typeTable.description: Number of the retry about to start. The first retry is `1`. For SSE and WebSocket the count restarts at `1` after a connection is established again.

typeTable.name: cause
typeTable.description: The failure that ended the attempt: a fault, an error, or the cause a WebSocket close carries. It is `undefined` when a WebSocket closed without one.

typeTable.name: retryable
typeTable.description: What the default policy decides for this failure: the method is in `methods` and the failure is one the transport retries by default. `shouldRetry` can return it as is or override it.

name: OutlierDetectionOptions
description:
Failure counting that ejects an endpoint for a while, and an optional
application-defined health check.
The library does not know what healthy means. It counts classified failures,
ejects an endpoint by time, and puts it back when the time is up (or admits
one probe at a time when `halfOpen` is enabled); only `isHealthy` can say
that an endpoint is unfit, and only the application supplies it. No timers,
settlement grid, or slow start are used.

typeTable.name: consecutiveFailures
typeTable.description: Consecutive failures that eject an endpoint; defaults to 5 (Finagle). Zero disables passive breaking.

typeTable.name: minPenaltyMs
typeTable.description: First penalty in milliseconds, also the step added per level; defaults to 1000 ms (Linkerd).

typeTable.name: maxPenaltyMs
typeTable.description: Penalty cap in milliseconds, at least `minPenaltyMs`; defaults to 60000 ms (Linkerd).

typeTable.name: jitterRatio
typeTable.description: Jitter ratio from 0 to 1; defaults to 0.5 (Linkerd).

typeTable.name: isFailure
typeTable.description:
Synchronous rule that decides which outcomes count toward ejection. The
default counts every outcome with a `code`. It is a trigger for time-based
ejection, not a judgement of health; replace it to count differently. A
throw is not caught here; it leaves `done` and is contained and reported
like any other `done` failure.

typeTable.name: isHealthy
typeTable.description:
The only health judgement. Synchronous, called on every pick for each
endpoint that is not currently ejected (an ejected endpoint is not asked),
so it should read state that the application keeps up to date. An
endpoint for which it returns `false` is not selected. Returning `true`
does not end an ejection: the endpoint must also not be ejected. A throw is
not caught here; `pickEndpoint` reports it as `REQ_BUILD_FAILED` with the
thrown value as `cause`.

typeTable.name: halfOpen
typeTable.description:
When `true`, an endpoint whose ejection penalty has expired admits only one
trial request at a time until that probe settles; a successful probe restores
full traffic and a failed probe immediately re-ejects the endpoint with the
next penalty level. Defaults to `false`.

typeTable.name: maxEjectionPercent
typeTable.description:
Maximum percentage of candidate endpoints that may be ejected at once, in
`[0, 100]`. Defaults to `100` (no quota; fail-open still applies when every
endpoint is ejected).

name: P2cOptions
description: Options for {@link p2cBalancer}.

typeTable.name: load
typeTable.description: Load signal: `"peakEwma"` (default) or `"pending"` in-flight attempts.

typeTable.name: choiceCount
typeTable.description: Number of candidates sampled, at least 2 and capped at 10; defaults to 2.

typeTable.name: defaultRttMs
typeTable.description: Initial RTT estimate in milliseconds; defaults to 30.

typeTable.name: decayMs
typeTable.description: RTT decay time in milliseconds; defaults to 10000.

typeTable.name: outlierDetection
typeTable.description: Health filtering; off by default. `{}` enables the defaults.

name: PickFaultCode
description:
Neutral attempt outcome codes observed through `end` and `done`.

`end` reports the beginning of a peer response; later failures can still give
`done` a different `code`. Unavailability and server failures describe a peer
that answered, while unreachable and timeout outcomes describe transport failures.
Normal completion and application errors do not themselves create failure samples.

Transport mapping: HTTP and SSE statuses 502, 503, and 504 map to
`NET_UNAVAILABLE`; other statuses at least 500 map to `NET_SERVER_ERROR`.
Incomplete HTTP bodies retain `NET_BODY_INCOMPLETE` and their status.
An SSE body-read rejection, a WebSocket heartbeat acknowledgement timeout,
or an opened WebSocket's close code 1006 or 1015 (no close frame arrived)
maps to `NET_UNREACHABLE`, without a status; a WebSocket close frame with
1012 or 1013 maps to `NET_UNAVAILABLE`, even when the engine dispatched no
`open` event before it; both unless timeout or cancellation takes priority.
Other close codes are not failures, whatever `wasClean` reports: engines
disagree on it for a server-initiated close.

overloads.signature:
type PickFaultCode =
  | "NET_UNREACHABLE"
  | "NET_UNAVAILABLE"
  | "NET_SERVER_ERROR"
  | "NET_TIMEOUT"
  | "NET_BODY_INCOMPLETE";

name: PickFirstOptions
description: Options for {@link pickFirstBalancer}.

typeTable.name: outlierDetection
typeTable.description: Health filtering around the sticky order; off by default. `{}` enables the defaults.

typeTable.name: shuffle
typeTable.description: Random but stable endpoint order instead of list order; defaults to `false`.

typeTable.name: failbackMs
typeTable.description: Milliseconds away from the first endpoint after which the next pick returns to it; unset disables failback.

name: PickInfo
description:
What the runtime tells `pick` about this call.

`endpoints` is the candidate list in first-seen order. It may be empty and
must not be modified. An empty list returns `[ERR_NO_CANDIDATE, undefined]`.
A retry picks again from every endpoint. Only a wrapping balancer that
filters candidates can make the list shorter than the client's endpoint list.

`members` is the client's whole endpoint list, the same for every attempt.
A narrower `endpoints` is a per-pick filter, not a membership change, so
balancers that keep order or per-endpoint state key it on `members`.

typeTable.name: endpoints
typeTable.description: Candidate endpoints for this pick. Already deduplicated by first occurrence. Do not modify.

typeTable.name: members
typeTable.description: Every client endpoint, a superset of `endpoints`. Absent means `endpoints`. Do not modify.

typeTable.name: meta
typeTable.description: `meta` from the definition, when it has one: the same object for every pick of every call. Read-only; never sent with the request.

name: PickOutcome
description:
Error-first result of {@link Balancer.pick}.

`[Error, undefined]` selects nothing. `[null, result]` is the selected
endpoint. The error comes first, matching operation results.

name: PickResult
description:
Endpoint selected for one call.

`done` is optional. When present, the runtime calls it once, synchronously,
with the outcome of this pick, or `{ attempted: false }` when no attempt can
be attributed to the endpoint.

The runtime reads `start`, `end`, and `done` once, when the pick returns, and
calls each without a receiver, so `this` is `undefined`. Use arrow functions,
closures, or bound functions for state. A synchronous throw does not change
the attempt or the operation tuple. It is reported with `reportError` where
the runtime defines it, and that can end a Bun or Deno process that has no
error handler. Where the runtime has no `reportError`, as in Node.js, the
throw stays contained. A returned promise is not awaited.

typeTable.name: endpoint
typeTable.description: One of this pick's candidate endpoints.

typeTable.name: start
typeTable.description:
Called synchronously at most once immediately before the attempt begins.
Not called for build failures, interceptor short-circuits, or pre-transport cancellation.
A throw is contained exactly like `done`.

typeTable.name: end
typeTable.description:
Called synchronously at most once after start, when the peer response begins,
or when transport fails before that response. Caller cancellation is unattributed,
and so is a network error on a streamed HTTP request body.
A throw is contained exactly like `done`.

typeTable.name: done
typeTable.description:
Called once with the attempt outcome. Omit when the balancer keeps no per-pick state.
Must be synchronous: a returned promise is not awaited.
A throw does not replace the operation tuple; it is reported as described above.

name: QuerySerializer
description:
Serializes an encoded query object into a query string.

`query` is the wire object: aliases already applied, `Date` values already ISO strings, `bigint` values already strings. Nested objects and arrays are preserved. The string is parsed into the request's `query`, a `URLSearchParams`, and the request sends `query.toString()`, the URL Standard's application/x-www-form-urlencoded serialization, so a space is `+` and the bytes the serializer wrote are not kept.

Set it with `withQuerySerializer`. Without one, queries use `URLSearchParams`: arrays repeat keys and a nested object fails. A builder that returns `URLSearchParams` skips the serializer.
returns: The query string without a leading `?`.

overloads.signature: type QuerySerializer = (query: { [key: string]: unknown }) => string;

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Encoded query object.

name: RequestOptions
description:
Flat per-call options. Each protocol reads the fields it understands and ignores the rest.

`signal` cancels HTTP, SSE, and WebSocket calls. `retry` applies to all three and replaces the client's retry policy for that call as a whole value, except its `budget`, which is HTTP only and stays with the client. `onUploadProgress` and `onDownloadProgress` apply to HTTP. `beforeConnect`, `protocols`, and `heartbeat` apply to WebSocket and replace the client setting for that call as a whole value. `client(options)` copies `heartbeat`, `retry`, and a `protocols` array at that call. Missing nested blocks stay missing. `signal`, `beforeConnect`, and callbacks keep their identity. There is no `timeout` or `abort` field. Pass `AbortSignal.timeout(ms)` as `signal` when a call needs a deadline.

typeTable.name: signal
typeTable.description: Aborts the call. An already aborted signal fails the call before transport.

typeTable.name: onUploadProgress
typeTable.description: Observes HTTP upload progress.

typeTable.name: onDownloadProgress
typeTable.description: Observes HTTP download progress.

typeTable.name: beforeConnect
typeTable.description: Runs before each WebSocket connect attempt for this call.
typeTable.type: ((context: { attempt: number; signal: AbortSignal; }) => void | Promise<void>) | undefined

typeTable.name: protocols
typeTable.description: WebSocket subprotocols for this call. Replaces the client list; it is not appended.

typeTable.name: heartbeat
typeTable.description: WebSocket heartbeat for this call. Replaces the client heartbeat as a whole value.

typeTable.name: retry
typeTable.description: Retry policy for this call, for HTTP, SSE, and WebSocket. Replaces the client policy as a whole value; the `budget` stays with the client.

name: RetryContext
description: Failure description passed to `shouldRetry`. Narrow it with `transport`.

overloads.signature:
type RetryContext =
  HttpRetryContext | SSERetryContext | WebSocketRetryContext;

name: RetryOptions
description:
Opt-in retry policy for HTTP, SSE, and WebSocket.

Call {@link withRetry}() or pass `{}` to enable retries with the defaults. Without a policy every call makes one attempt. Per call, `client({ retry })` replaces the client's policy as a whole value.

After each failed attempt the policy decides in this order:

1. A caller abort, a manual `close()`, a fatal error such as a mismatched media type, a WebSocket whose constructor throws, and a `ReadableStream` request body end the call. `shouldRetry` is not called.
2. When `retryAfter` is enabled and a `429` or `503` response carries a valid `Retry-After` delay exceeding `maxRetryAfterMs`, the call ends immediately without calling `shouldRetry` or spending `budget`.
3. When `maxRetries` retries have been made, the call ends. `shouldRetry` is not called.
4. `shouldRetry(context)` decides. Without it, `context.retryable` does.
5. HTTP only: a retry that the `budget` cannot pay for ends the call.
6. The call waits for the `Retry-After` delay (when present on a `429` or `503` response and enabled, with positive jitter up to `maxRetryAfterMs`) or the exponential backoff delay, then the balancer picks an endpoint again. Every endpoint is a candidate, including the one that just failed, so a single endpoint is tried again after the delay.

typeTable.name: maxRetries
typeTable.description: Retries after the first attempt. Defaults to 3; `0` never retries. For SSE and WebSocket the count restarts when a connection is established again.

typeTable.name: delayMs
typeTable.description: Initial backoff delay in milliseconds. Defaults to 1000. Zero skips waiting.

typeTable.name: factor
typeTable.description: Multiplier applied to the delay for each further retry. Defaults to 2. The first retry waits `delayMs`.

typeTable.name: maxDelayMs
typeTable.description: Cap on the final delay in milliseconds, jitter included. Defaults to 30000; `Infinity` removes the cap. The platform timer limit of `2_147_483_647` still applies.

typeTable.name: jitter
typeTable.description: Multiplicative jitter in [0, 1]. Defaults to 0.2, plus or minus twenty percent for exponential backoff, or positive-only `[1, 1 + jitter]` for `Retry-After`.

typeTable.name: attemptTimeoutMs
typeTable.description:
Time limit for one attempt in milliseconds. Unset by default. HTTP counts from the call to the end of the response body, SSE to the response headers, WebSocket to `open`. An attempt that runs out is a failure that the policy handles like a connection failure.
Use `withRetry({ maxRetries: 0, attemptTimeoutMs })` for a time limit without retries.

typeTable.name: methods
typeTable.description: Methods the default policy retries, case-insensitive. Defaults to GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT, and DELETE. HTTP checks every method an attempt sent, after interceptor rewrites. WebSocket ignores it.

typeTable.name: statusCodes
typeTable.description: HTTP and SSE non-2xx status codes retried by default. Defaults to `[429, 502, 503, 504]`. WebSocket ignores it.

typeTable.name: retryAfter
typeTable.description: Whether to honor the RFC 9110 `Retry-After` header on `429` and `503` HTTP and SSE handshake responses. Defaults to `true`.

typeTable.name: maxRetryAfterMs
typeTable.description: Maximum `Retry-After` delay in milliseconds that the policy will wait. Defaults to `60000`; `Infinity` removes the cap (platform timer cap still applies). A longer server-requested delay ends the call immediately without waiting or drawing from `budget`.

typeTable.name: shouldRetry
typeTable.description: Decides whether a failed attempt is retried. It is called after the `maxRetries` check and replaces `context.retryable`; return it to keep the default. It may return a promise, which the caller's signal can cancel. A throw ends the call with `EXT_HOOK_FAILED` and the thrown value as `cause`; an open SSE stream reports that code in `closed.code`, and an open WebSocket session ends with `closed.kind: "error"` and the thrown value as `closed.cause`.

typeTable.name: budget
typeTable.description:
HTTP only. Client-owned Finagle retry budget; `false` removes the cap.
Derived clients sharing one configuration share its budget. Separate clients
keep independent budgets, even when they share a balancer. Credits and debits
expire lazily in ten TTL/10 slices (at most one slice early).
Defaults: 20% plus 10 retries/second of reserve over a 10000 ms TTL.
typeTable.type: false | { readonly percentCanRetry?: number; readonly minRetriesPerSecond?: number; readonly ttlMs?: number; } | undefined

name: RoundRobinOptions
description: Options for {@link roundRobinBalancer}.

typeTable.name: outlierDetection
typeTable.description: Health filtering; off by default. `{}` enables the defaults.

typeTable.name: weights
typeTable.description: Finite positive weight per endpoint; a missing weight is 1. Copied at construction.

name: SSERetryContext
description:
What `shouldRetry` receives after an SSE handshake or stream failed.

`cause` is the failure: an `HTTP_STATUS` fault for a non-2xx handshake, otherwise the error that ended the attempt. `retryable` is `true` for a method in `methods` and a handshake network failure, a handshake status in `statusCodes` (429, 502, 503, or 504 by default), an attempt timeout, or a network error after the stream opened. A normal end of the stream never retries.

typeTable.name: method
typeTable.description: Method of the stream request.

typeTable.name: lastEventId

name: WebSocketHandle
description:
Minimal WebSocket instance surface used by the client transport.

It is the DOM `WebSocket` without its event-handler properties, `binaryType`, `dispatchEvent`, and the state constants. A custom implementation therefore needs `url`, `protocol`, `extensions`, `bufferedAmount`, `send`, `close`, `addEventListener`, `removeEventListener`, and a numeric `readyState`.

The transport sets `binaryType = 'arraybuffer'` when the property exists and ignores its absence. If the setter throws, it requests best-effort closure of the constructed handle before failing that attempt with `NET_UNREACHABLE`; the socket is not left outside cleanup. When the transport stops listening to a handle's `error` event, it leaves a no-op `error` listener that it never removes, so an implementation that throws for an `error` event without listeners (an `EventEmitter`-based one such as `ws` does when it is closed while connecting) cannot crash the process after the transport has detached its own listeners. This property is an optimization, and the decoder also accepts Blob frames. This is the instance type produced by a {@link WebSocketHandleConstructor}.

type WebSocketHandle = Omit<
  WebSocket,
  | "binaryType"
  | "CLOSED"
  | "CLOSING"
  | "CONNECTING"
  | "dispatchEvent"
  | "onclose"
  | "onerror"
  | "onmessage"
  | "onopen"
  | "OPEN"
  | "readyState"
> & { readonly readyState: number };
